title: Ch 11 Test: Electricity
subject: Science
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Internal choice is given in some questions.
Section A: 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 5 marks. Section E: case-based, 4 marks.
In numericals, write the formula, substitute values with units, and give the final answer with its unit.

questions.q: A wire of resistance R is cut into five equal parts, which are then connected in parallel. If the equivalent resistance is R′, the ratio R/R′ is:
questions.answer: (d) 25. Each part is R/5, and five in parallel give R′ = R/25.

questions.q: Which of the following does NOT represent electric power in a circuit?
The SI unit of electric charge is the:
How much current does an 1100 W appliance draw from a 220 V supply?
An electric bulb is rated 220 V, 100 W. When it is operated on 110 V, the power consumed is:

**Assertion (A):** An ammeter is always connected in series with the component whose current is to be measured.
**Reason (R):** The same current flows through all components connected in series.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q: How much work is done in moving a charge of 2 C across two points that have a potential difference of 12 V?

or.q: Why are the coils of electric toasters and electric irons made of an alloy rather than a pure metal?
or.answer: Alloys have a higher resistivity than pure metals, so they produce more heat. They also do not oxidise (burn) easily at high temperatures.

questions.q: Resistors of 4 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in series to a 12 V battery. Find the current in the circuit and the potential difference across the 4 Ω resistor.
A copper wire has a diameter of 0.5 mm and a resistivity of 1.6 × 10^{-8} Ω m.

subparts.q: What length of this wire will have a resistance of 10 Ω?
If the diameter is doubled (same length), how does the resistance change?
subparts.answer: The area becomes 4 times, so the resistance becomes one-fourth (2.5 Ω).

questions.q: Three resistors of 5 Ω, 10 Ω and 30 Ω are connected in parallel to a 12 V battery.

subparts.q: Find the current through each resistor.
Find the total current drawn from the battery.

subparts.answer: The heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance, and the time for which the current flows: H = I^{2}Rt.

subparts.q: An electric iron of resistance 20 Ω takes a current of 5 A. Calculate the heat produced in 30 s.
Two lamps, one rated 100 W at 220 V and the other 60 W at 220 V, are connected in parallel to a 220 V supply. What current is drawn from the supply?

or.q:
(a) Why is a parallel arrangement used in domestic wiring rather than a series arrangement? Give two reasons. [2]
(b) An electric refrigerator rated 400 W runs 8 hours a day. What is the cost of the energy it uses in 30 days at ₹3.00 per kWh? [3]
or.answer: (a) In parallel, each appliance gets the full supply voltage, and each can be switched on or off independently. If one appliance fails, the others keep working. (b) Energy = 0.4 kW × 8 h × 30 = 96 kWh. Cost = 96 × ₹3.00 = ₹288.

sections.title: Section E
sections.note: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: In an experiment, a student measured the current (I) through a resistor for different potential differences (V). The readings were: I = 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 A and V = 1.6, 3.4, 6.7, 10.2, 13.2 V respectively.

subparts.q: What relationship between V and I do these readings show?
subparts.answer: V is directly proportional to I (Ohm's law). The V–I graph is a straight line through the origin.

subparts.q: Calculate the resistance using the reading I = 2.0 A.
The resistor is replaced by a wire of the same material and thickness but double the length. What current will flow at 6.7 V?
subparts.answer: Resistance is proportional to length, so R doubles to about 6.7 Ω. I = V/R = 6.7/6.7 ≈ 1.0 A
